name: bumble-7fdeef5c-blind30-ots
instr:
# Bumble Bluetooth stack: 30 injected faults to diagnose without a test suite

An application built on this library joins two radio stacks together, learns what the far end can do, and carries audio and control traffic between them, and it now gets a great many of those things wrong. Nothing about the radio standards changed and nothing about my calling code changed; the same sequences that used to complete now hang, are refused outright, or come back with the wrong answer. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Everything below is what I have been able to observe from the outside.

Joining two stacks over a plain stream socket and then pointing one at the other no longer works. The power-up sequence at the connecting end never finishes, and at the accepting end the inbound and outbound halves of the link look to have been handed over in the wrong order, so nothing the emulated controller writes ever finds its way back. Asking for a connecting-side link to an IPv6 loopback address goes wrong on its own account, separately from that hang, while the plain IPv4 spelling at least gets as far as hanging. The same exercise over a web socket stalls at power-up for both address families with the two halves likewise exchanged, and on top of that an accepting end asked for at an IPv6 loopback address is not brought up the way the IPv4 one is.
